title: August and the Songbook
premise: August Reyes, a baker counting down the days until his bakery lease expires, is assigned an anonymous pen-pal through a community program meant to pair strangers—only to discover his correspondent is Petra Lockridge, the sharp-tongued marine biologist whose family trust owns his building and wants him out. As their letters deepen into something neither will admit to, August learns the Lockridge inheritance hinges on converting the waterfront block into a research facility, with Petra as its reluctant face. When their identities are exposed at a public hearing, duty and love collide: Petra must choose between the legacy she was trained to protect and the man she trained herself never to need. In the end, she rewrites the trust's terms to preserve the bakery, and August leaves the door unlocked long after the last train has gone.
about_author: M. M. Winterbourne is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper columnist who spent a decade writing obituaries and wedding announcements, and swears they taught her everything about love. She now lives in a coastal town much like the one in this book, where she keeps a bakery on speed dial.

chapters.title: The Last Train Schedule
chapters.summary: August's POV. Facing eviction by the Lockridge Trust in ninety days, August grudgingly joins a community pen-pal program at his sister's urging, venting about landlords to an anonymous stranger. His first letter is bitter and funny; the reply he receives is unexpectedly kind. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as practicality begins to crack.

chapters.title: Saltwater Correspondence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Letters fly back and forth through autumn: August confesses his father's lost songbook of bakery tunes, while 'P' admits she counts turtles to avoid counting what she owes her family. In town, August and Petra spar over the lease without knowing they're falling for each other on paper. Emotional beat: intimacy grows in the space anonymity provides.

chapters.title: What the Trust Requires
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At a public hearing on the waterfront redevelopment, a misdelivered letter exposes both identities before the whole town—and Petra's grandmother, who controls the trust. Humiliated and cornered, Petra votes to proceed with demolition, and August burns her letters. Emotional beat: betrayal, pride, and the wreckage of choosing duty over truth.

chapters.title: Stay After Closing
chapters.summary: August's POV, closing with Petra's. On the lease's final night, Petra arrives with the amended trust documents—she has restructured her inheritance to save the block, forfeiting her grandmother's approval—and August's father's songbook, which she secretly had restored. He plays the last tune; she stays after closing. Emotional beat: love chosen freely over legacy imposed.
